label: D1 after an unrewarded visit to S2, when the agent leans to a1
explanation: Fires almost only at D1 (97% of activation mass, never at GO). It fires when the previous trial ended in S2 without reward (prev_state != 1 also lets in the first trial of the window, where prev_state is unknown) and the policy logit at that step favors a1 (choice > 0). That is the model-based case of shifting away from S2: either a1 after a rare S2 (stay) or a2 after a common S2 (switch to a1). It is silent after unrewarded visits to S1 and after rewarded trials, and it never fires at GO. Using the upcoming action (action == 1) in place of choice > 0 gives P 0.93 / R 0.71 / F1 0.81 on dev, and dropping the choice condition drops precision to 0.55. Both choice and action are the agent own computed choice, not a future outcome. The predicate misses weak activations (lowest quartile): D1 after rewarded trials (about 0.1-0.26 of max) and some D2 steps following chains of unrewarded trials. Activations inside the predicate are near max (about 0.9-1.0).

issues: All the factual claims hold. GO activity is exactly 0 (P/R 0 for phase==GO). D1 holds 0.973 of activation mass. After an unrewarded visit to S1 the unit never fires (prev_state==1 & prev_reward==0 at D1: 0 of 51338, including when choice>0). After a rewarded trial the D1 firing rate is 0.7%. The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.852, R 0.802, F1 0.827, MR 0.954.

The two sub-cases are presented as equal, but they are not. Rare a1->S2 unrewarded (prev_action==1 & prev_state==2 & prev_reward==0 at D1) scores P 0.999 / R 0.478 / MR 0.666 on dev (test P 0.999, MR 0.646), and choice>0 adds nothing there (only 5 such steps have choice<=0). Common a2->S2 unrewarded is weaker. It has P 0.31 alone and P 0.805 with choice>0, holding only about 11-14% of mass, and it fires reliably only when the lean to a1 is strong (choice>1: P 0.989). So the unit mostly codes 'unrewarded after a rare transition from a1'. The choice gate matters only for the a2-common and unknown-history cases.

There is one systematic false-positive source: the window's first trial, where prev_state==-1. There the predicate has P 0.64 (test 0.62) and carries about 17% of mass. These steps presumably mix in unseen prev-S1 histories, so this is a limitation of the data window, not an error in the concept.

The misses are weak, scattered activations: the lowest quartile, about 4.6% of mass on test. They are D1 after rewarded trials (about 0.1-0.3 of max) and some D2 steps where action==1 (D2 P about 0.12, 2.7% mass). None of these forms a large class.
A slightly tighter choice threshold improves precision with negligible loss: choice>0.5 gives test P 0.897 / R 0.788 / F1 0.839. This is a marginal gain, not a refutation.
